result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.count_selected_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get count of currently selected edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6191-L6221){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns the number of edges currently marked as selected. More efficient than `len(get_selected_edges())` when you only need the count. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of selected edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} As with `get_selected_edge_ids()`, this cycle has no explicit weights, so every edge's `weight` is `None` and the count comes back `0`: ::: {#b52d76eb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_cycle_graph(n=10) .select_edges(lambda e: e.weight is not None and e.weight > 0.7) ) graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0 ``` ::: :::
